stem: Kinematics, as introduced in this chapter, is the study of
options: the causes of motion, such as forces
ways to describe motion without its causes
the motion of extended rigid bodies
explanation: Correct option: (B). Kinematics describes motion (position, velocity, acceleration) without going into its causes. The causes (forces) are studied later in the laws of motion; energy and rigid bodies are separate topics.

stem: A body in motion can be treated as a point object when
options: its mass is very small compared with 1 kg
it moves with a constant velocity
its size is much smaller than the distance it moves
it moves only along a vertical line
explanation: Correct option: (C). The point-object approximation holds when the size of the object is much smaller than the distance it covers in a reasonable time. Mass, constant velocity or the direction of motion do not decide this.

stem: A man walks 40 m east along a straight road in 20 s and then 20 m back west in 10 s. What are his average speed and the magnitude of his average velocity for the whole trip?
explanation: Correct option: (D). Total path length = 40 + 20 = 60 m and total time = 30 s, so average speed = 60/30 = 2 m/s. Net displacement = 40 - 20 = 20 m east, so average velocity = 20/30 = 2/3 m/s. Equal values ignore the return trip; 2/3 and 2 swaps the two quantities; 3 and 1 use wrong totals.

stem:
Assertion (A): Over any time interval, the average speed of an object is greater than or equal to the magnitude of its average velocity.
Reason (R): The total path length covered is never less than the magnitude of the displacement.
options: Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true and Reason (R) is the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
Both Assertion (A) and Reason (R) are true, but Reason (R) is not the correct explanation of Assertion (A).
Assertion (A) is true, but Reason (R) is false.
Assertion (A) is false, but Reason (R) is true.
explanation: Correct option: (A). Average speed = path length/time and |average velocity| = |displacement|/time. Since the path length is at least the magnitude of the displacement (equal only for motion in one direction), A follows directly from R.

stem: A body moves along the x-axis and returns to its starting point after 10 s, having covered a total path of 50 m. Which statement about the 10 s interval is correct?
options: Average velocity is 5 m/s and average speed is zero.
Average velocity is zero and average speed is 5 m/s.
Both average velocity and average speed are zero.
Both average velocity and average speed are 5 m/s.
explanation: Correct option: (B). Returning to the start means zero displacement, so average velocity = 0. Average speed = 50 m/10 s = 5 m/s, which is not zero because a path was covered. The other options confuse displacement with path length.

stem: Instantaneous velocity of a particle moving along x is defined as
options: the limit of x/t as t becomes very large
the limit of delta x/delta t as delta t tends to zero
the total distance divided by the total time
the change in velocity divided by the time taken
explanation: Correct option: (B). v = lim (delta x / delta t) as delta t tends to 0, that is dx/dt. Total distance by total time is average speed; change in velocity per time is acceleration; x/t for large t is not a definition of velocity.

stem: On a position-time (x-t) graph, the velocity of a particle at a given instant equals
options: the area under the curve up to that instant
the slope of the chord from the origin to that point
the slope of the tangent to the curve at that instant
the value of x read off at that instant
explanation: Correct option: (C). Instantaneous velocity is the slope of the tangent to the x-t curve at that instant. The chord slope gives an average velocity, the area under an x-t curve has no such meaning, and x itself is the position.

stem: A car starts from rest, accelerates uniformly to 20 m/s in 10 s, moves at 20 m/s for 10 s and then stops uniformly in 10 s. How far does it travel in all?
explanation: Correct option: (A). The v-t graph is a trapezium. Area = (1/2)(10)(20) + (10)(20) + (1/2)(10)(20) = 100 + 200 + 100 = 400 m. 600 m treats the whole 30 s at 20 m/s; 200 m counts only the middle part; 300 m drops one triangle.

stem: Taking the upward direction as positive, a ball falls freely downward. Which statement about its motion is correct?
options: Acceleration is negative, so its speed decreases.
Acceleration is positive, so its speed increases.
Acceleration is negative, yet its speed increases.
Acceleration is zero, as it is in free fall.
explanation: Correct option: (C). With up as positive, g acts downward so a = -9.8 m s^-2. The velocity is also downward (negative), so acceleration and velocity point the same way and the speed increases. The sign of acceleration alone does not tell whether the speed rises or falls.

stem: The kinematic equations v = v0 + at and x = v0t + (1/2)at^2 are valid only when
options: the velocity of the body is constant
the acceleration is constant in size and direction
the body starts its motion from rest
the body moves vertically under gravity
explanation: Correct option: (B). These equations are derived for one-dimensional motion with uniform (constant) acceleration. Constant velocity is only the special case a = 0; starting from rest or vertical motion are not required.

stem: A car moving at 126 km/h is brought to rest in a distance of 200 m with uniform retardation. What is the magnitude of its retardation?
explanation: Correct option: (A). 126 km/h = 35 m/s. Using v^2 = v0^2 + 2ax with v = 0: a = -(35^2)/(2 x 200) = -1225/400 = -3.06 m s^-2. 6.13 omits the factor 2; 39.7 uses 126 without converting to m/s; 0.31 is a decimal-place slip.

stem: Neglecting air resistance, an object released from rest near the earth's surface moves with
options: an acceleration that rises as it falls
an acceleration that depends on its mass
a constant downward acceleration of 9.8 m s^-2
explanation: Correct option: (D). In free fall the only acceleration is g, about 9.8 m s^-2 downward, the same for all objects and constant near the surface. Its velocity changes, so it is not constant; g does not depend on mass or increase as the object falls.

explanation: Correct option: (B). Stopping distance d = v0^2/(2a), so it is proportional to the square of the initial speed. Doubling v0 makes d four times larger, not twice, half or the same.

stem: A ball is thrown vertically upward with a speed of 29.4 m/s (take g = 9.8 m s^-2). What is the maximum height it reaches?

explanation: Correct option: (D). The ruler falls freely from rest: d = (1/2)g t^2, so t = sqrt(2d/g) = sqrt(2 x 0.21/9.8) = sqrt(0.0429) = 0.21 s. 0.04 s forgets the square root; 0.15 s omits the factor 2; 0.46 s is just the square root of 0.21 without using g.
